radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Date: 15 Jan 2025 | Institution: Catharina Ziekenhuis (Eindhoven)

Clinical Context:
A 67-year-old gentleman with a PSA reading of 6.0 ng/mL and a history of a negative biopsy warrants re-evaluation due to a rising PSA trajectory and clinical suspicion of clinically significant prostate cancer.

Imaging Characteristics:
The gland occupies 79.0 mL of volume. T2-weighted sequences highlight a focal hypointense abnormality, roughly 18 mm, situated in the right peripheral zone at mid-gland height. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction with matching low apparent diffusion coefficient signal. Dynamic contrast phases capture early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent parenchyma. Seminal vesicles remain clear; no capsular breach or suspicious nodal enlargement is evident. Bladder and distal urethra appear intact.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right peripheral zone mid-gland.
Prostate volume 79.0 mL; PSA density 0.08 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7697653.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial laboratory screening identified a PSA level of 3.9 ng/mL. Digital palpation showed no abnormalities. A multiparametric MRI was ordered to evaluate potential suspicious areas. After reviewing the risks associated with a biopsy, the patient opted to pursue imaging first.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: Subsequent laboratory analysis conducted in June 2024 indicated a PSA rise to 5.4 ng/mL. Earlier imaging had identified a PI-RADS 4 lesion, prompting a systematic biopsy that ultimately yielded negative results for cancer. Owing to the sustained PSA elevation alongside those radiological markers, the individual is being redirected to urology for further assessment.
